posts.text: Invent inexpensive, efficient 100-hour electricity storage with a complete reversible physical cycle.

Can a new material, electrochemical mechanism or storage architecture provide multi-day dispatchable electricity with genuinely low complete cost, useful efficiency and sustainable life? Develop the whole electricity-in/electricity-out operation. The mechanism is your choice; iron chemistry is an available starting point, not a restriction or a supplied battery.Use a nominal 100 W net regulated AC module that delivers continuously for 100 hours after a 144-hour hold. Define 10 kWh as the USEFUL energy actually delivered at the oad after that hold, rather than active-material theoretical energy. Charge in at most 100 hours with peak imported power at most twice rated output. Specify a practical AC interface and power-quality limits. Ordinary ambient air is 20--35 degrees Celsius with 20--80 percent relative humidity; no free temperature-controlled room, pure oxygen/nitrogen supply or external hot/cold utility is provided. Internal heating, cooling, atmosphere control, pumping, gas processing and electronics must be actual paid components.Target at least 65-percent AC-to-AC round-trip efficiency over the complete charge/hold/discharge operation. Meter all imported and exported electricity, initial/final state of charge, chemical and thermal inventories, standby, formation, control, water/gas handling and reset. A clean uncharged state must be attainable; starting with an uncharged label but a fuel-bearing metal or mediator is not a complete balance. Define the useful state window, startup and safe shutdown, partial discharge and repeated operation. Show a fixed physical design with credible tolerance and aging margins rather than enlarging an ideal part after each unfavorable case.At a 100 kW/10 MWh reference installation and a credible manufacturing volume, target all-in installed capital at most US$15 per useful delivered kWh. Pay active and inactive materials, synthesis/refining, additives, electrode preparation and formation, separators, gas electrodes or other interfaces, tanks/frames, power conversion sized for BOTH charging and discharge, air/water equipment, controls, transport, installation, yield, quality assurance, containment and waste. Price the first nominal module and a smaller decisive prototype separately. A commodity raw-material price is not a quote for a qualified active material or a factory.For a complete delivered-energy comparison, evaluate the full 100-hour-charge/144-hour-hold/100-hour-discharge schedule, 90-percent availability, 20-year financial horizon and 8-percent real discount rate. Include actual degradation, replacements, calendar effects, maintenance, energy, site/labour, waste and decommissioning. The complete-cost target is at most US$125 per MWh delivered AC at charging electricity US$20/MWh. Also calculate the same operation at US$40/MWh and under lower annual use. A component life shorter than the financial horizon is allowed only with its paid replacement and lost availability; the horizon does not grant a 20-year material life.All mechanisms are open: electrochemical storage, redox flow, a different chemical cycle, thermal/mechanical storage or another physically consistent architecture. Choose actual constituents, manufacturing and operating conditions. Recharging must restore the useful energy-bearing states, including any mediator, sulfide, electrolyte, gas inventory or off-site regeneration. Count consumed chemical feedstocks, replacement materials and their preparation rather than naming them catalysts. Captured heat, sunlight, hydrogen or another energy source must have an explicit accounting boundary and cannot quietly replace the imported charging electricity.A real material construction supplies one possible opening. Manohar, Yang and Narayanan's 2015 alkaline iron-electrode study hot-pressed carbonyl iron with additives/binder onto nickel grids and tested it in 30 wt-percent KOH. Iron sulfide plus bismuth oxide suppressed passivation and maintained high electrode charge efficiency during extended cycling; a bismuth-sulfide-only formulation suffered capacity fade associated with loss of sulfide and magnetite accumulation. The counter electrode was nickel oxide, not a demonstrated reversible air electrode. These results supply useful phase/transport/manufacturing ideas, not a full 100-hour store, AC efficiency, free pure iron, calendar life or a plant cost. They also show why an additive reservoir and its loss must be paid. You may develop a different opening.Optional primary starting source: [https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/52ce/c227d5660ed836f69c2cfca6031f58ad1011.pdf](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/52ce/c227d5660ed836f69c2cfca6031f58ad1011.pdf) , DOI10.1149/2.0741509jes, particularly Experimental, the different sulfide formulations and Results/Conclusions. Credit this existing work. You are free to investigate newer or different mechanisms rather than repeat its working-electrode experiment.A few conditional engineering screens may help identify a joint mechanism:- For a mean-voltage electrochemical surrogate, full efficiency is the product of charge/discharge power-conversion efficiencies, useful charge retention, hold retention, auxiliary factor and discharge-to-charge mean voltage ratio. Hypothetical 0.97/0.97 power stages, 0.98 cycling charge efficiency, 0.99 hold retention and 0.98 auxiliary factor leave a factor 0.8946 before voltage loss. To reach 65 percent, V_charge/V_discharge must then be at most 1.3763; a 0.9 V mean discharge permits about 1.239 V mean charge. These factors are unproved simultaneous properties, not supplied performance. Integrate actual current and voltage and avoid double counting retention already inside a measured efficiency.- In the two-electron Fe/Fe(OH)2 window, theoretical charge is about 960 Ah/kg Fe. With an illustrative 20-percent useful iron fraction, 0.9 V mean discharge and the above output/hold assumptions, a 100 kW/10 MWh store needs about 61.5 tonnes Fe. An UNQUOTED US$1/kg processed active-iron assumption alone costs US$6.15/useful kWh before other materials and hardware. High-purity carbonyl powder or another prepared electrode cannot simply be assigned a scrap-metal price.- Low current trades efficiency against area. Under the same hypothetical 100-hour duty, 1 mA/cm2 needs about 11,689 m2 active area for 100 kW. An UNQUOTED US$10/m2 electrochemical-area allowance already costs about US$11.69/useful kWh. Raising current to 10 mA/cm2 divides that area term by ten but requires about 52.6 kg Fe/m2 at the stated utilization. A hypothetical 50-percent iron-volume packing makes a 13.4 mm layer; at an introduced effective conductivity of 10 S/m its through-thickness drop is about 0.134 V. Actual access, porosity, phase change, passivation, transport and manufacture remain new. A flowing inventory or separation of power interface from bulk storage may change the model, but it requires a real mechanism and return path.

- The complete schedule takes 344 hours. At 90-percent availability it permits at most about 22.92 full cycles/year before additional downtime. At US$15/useful kWh, the stated financing contributes about US$66.66/MWh; an introduced 2-percent-capital annual maintenance adds US$13.09 and US$20 charging at 65 percent adds US$30.77. The subtotal US$110.52 excludes replacements, fade and other costs. Neither the capital target nor efficiency alone establishes the complete-cost target.Build a physical design and executable complete-cycle model that closes energy, matter, actual stored inventory and cost at the SAME operating point. For electrochemistry include both electrode reactions, actual oxygen/water/carbon dioxide exposure, hydrogen evolution or other parasitic currents, passivation and phase transitions, ionic/electronic transport, leakage/crossover, additive depletion, current distribution, heat and electrolyte changes. For another mechanism identify and pay the corresponding physical interfaces. Working-electrode Coulombic efficiency, peak polarization power, a shallow fast cycle or theoretical elemental capacity does not provide an integrated store.Compare the same useful charge window, hold time, delivered AC power/energy, ambient conditions, utilization and financial boundary against strong present lithium-ion, flow, metal-air, thermal, mechanical and other relevant storage. Focus on the strongest applicable alternatives rather than listing technologies. Distinguish actual measured systems, public planning targets, extrapolated short-duration data and unquoted cost scenarios. Do not compare this store with a deliberately inefficient converter or treat the low price of one element as an invention. Identify the new useful operation and the consequential full-system advantage it could supply; if an incumbent already meets this entire contract, seek a further meaningful capability.
